Course release dates and third-party mock-test timing do not define the exam's availability or duration. **VERIFY CURRENT:** exam logistics and assessment access.

proposed_changes.reason: Remove repeated stale claim from learning caveat; preserve original vendor/course search limitations.

depth_findings.wording: Connect to Copilot connectors

depth_findings.wording: Connect to Microsoft Power Platform connectors
depth_findings.reason: Real-time connector knowledge is named, but source selection, connection and table/filter setup are not worked.

depth_findings.wording: Add a tool by using an existing custom connector
depth_findings.reason: Existing custom connector is a decision-table choice; actual add/select operation and mappings are omitted.

depth_findings.wording: Add REST APIs to an agent
depth_findings.reason: REST tool schemas and backend permissions are taught; operation import/selection is not demonstrated.

depth_findings.wording: Integrate an existing agent in Copilot Studio
depth_findings.reason: Independent lifecycle and sharing are distinguished; no concrete existing-agent add/configuration path.

depth_findings.wording: Implement and extend Microsoft Power Platform Pipelines
depth_findings.reason: Stage/gate sequence is sound; extending a host with specific event/gated completion is omitted.

depth_findings.wording: Understand differences in capabilities between versions of Copilot
depth_findings.reason: Table names experiences but does not teach concrete current license/grounding differences.

depth_findings.wording: Understand capabilities of Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat web and mobile experiences
depth_findings.reason: Web/mobile parity is deferred to VERIFY CURRENT; no actual mobile behavior is taught.

depth_findings.wording: Understand capabilities of the Copilot experience in various Microsoft 365 apps
depth_findings.reason: Apps are listed together without app-specific capabilities or examples.

depth_findings.wording: Automate resource provisioning by using GitHub Actions workflows
depth_findings.reason: Workflow submits jobs rather than provisioning resources; infrastructure action remains prose only.

depth_findings.wording: Run model training scripts
depth_findings.reason: Scripts are required but an actual parameterized training invocation is not shown.

depth_findings.wording: Deploy infrastructure using Bicep templates and Azure CLI
depth_findings.reason: Bicep/CLI required but no Foundry resource deployment example/command is present.

depth_findings.wording: Deploy foundation models by using serverless API endpoints and managed compute options
depth_findings.reason: Deployment types are distinguished, but creating the chosen deployment remains high-level.

depth_findings.wording: Select and fine-tune embedding models for domain-specific use cases and accuracy improvements
depth_findings.reason: Embedding selection and reindexing are taught, but training an embedding model is absent.

depth_findings.wording: Respond to spoken prompts by using a deployed multimodal model
depth_findings.reason: Direct spoken model is described but no portal turn or request/session workflow is worked.

depth_findings.wording: Build a lightweight application by using Azure Speech in Foundry Tools
depth_findings.reason: Speech function consumes configured recognizer, but client/audio creation and synthesis remain omitted.

depth_findings.wording: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model
depth_findings.reason: Image attachment is described without actual content shape/API operation.

depth_findings.wording: Create new visual outputs by using generative models
depth_findings.reason: Separate generation operation is required but actual endpoint/body/output parsing is absent.

depth_findings.wording: Build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities
depth_findings.reason: Lightweight vision app steps are generic; no concrete client image payload.

depth_findings.wording: Extract information from documents and forms by using Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
depth_findings.reason: Analyzer/version/confidence decisions taught; no invoice submit/operation/result path is demonstrated.

depth_findings.wording: Extract information from images by using Content Understanding
depth_findings.reason: Images named in generic modality list but no analyzer and output example.

depth_findings.wording: Extract information from audio and video by using Content Understanding
depth_findings.reason: Audio/video named without their actual analyzer/transcript/keyframe response contracts.

depth_findings.wording: Build a lightweight application with information extraction capabilities by using Content Understanding
depth_findings.reason: Async polling described but no submission/status terminal-state implementation.

depth_findings.wording: Manage resource groups
depth_findings.reason: Resource group lifecycle grouping is described; management operation is thin beyond lab creation.

depth_findings.wording: Manage subscriptions
depth_findings.reason: Subscription boundary is defined without actual management/hierarchy change workflow.

depth_findings.wording: Configure management groups
depth_findings.reason: Management-group inheritance is described without create/move/permission workflow.

depth_findings.wording: Configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files
depth_findings.reason: Files snapshots/share soft delete are table entries without actual creation/restore workflow.

depth_findings.wording: Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
depth_findings.reason: Syntax names and deployment-mode behavior are explained but no ARM/Bicep resource example to interpret.

depth_findings.wording: Modify an existing Azure Resource Manager template
depth_findings.reason: Export cleanup and property reset warned; actual JSON parameter/property change is absent.

depth_findings.wording: Modify an existing Bicep file
depth_findings.reason: Bicep constructs named but no concrete modification/example.

depth_findings.wording: Deploy resources by using an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
depth_findings.reason: Build/what-if/deploy process is described but runnable command/resource artifact absent.

depth_findings.wording: Deploy and configure an Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
depth_findings.reason: Scale-set field list exists, but no worked creation, health or scaling path.

depth_findings.wording: Configure Azure DNS
depth_findings.reason: Public delegation/private links/hybrid forwarding described; no record-set change/validation example.

depth_findings.wording: Create a Recovery Services vault
depth_findings.reason: Two vault families and policy named, but no actual Recovery Services creation workflow.

depth_findings.wording: Create an Azure Backup vault
depth_findings.reason: Two vault families named, but Backup vault creation/settings are absent.

depth_findings.wording: Configure Azure Site Recovery for Azure resources
depth_findings.reason: ASR dependencies and isolated drill are taught; enabling replication remains thin.

depth_findings.wording: Perform a failover to a secondary region by using Site Recovery
depth_findings.reason: Only test failover is worked; full failover/commit/reprotect is missing.

depth_findings.wording: Configure and interpret reports and alerts for backups
depth_findings.reason: Generic monitoring is present, but backup-specific report collection, job deduplication and alert path are absent.

proposed_changes.old_text: The September documentation distinguishes public-cloud availability from Azure Government's phased redundant-TCP rollout and macOS **Beta** UDP support. Windows App version requirements also differ for multiple UDP paths and redundant TCP. Use the current [Multipath prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-multipath) for the exact client/cloud combination. Standby paths improve resilience; they do not promise summed bandwidth or survival when every network path is lost. TURN is a relay, so a UDP connection is not necessarily a direct client-to-host route.
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown: **VERIFY CURRENT — October 28, 2026:** The current [Multipath availability matrix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-multipath) marks multiple UDP and redundant TCP paths generally available in both public Azure and Azure Government. The Government endpoint tab separately labels RDP Shortpath through its listed endpoints public preview and limits it to designated validation rings; that narrower endpoint rollout does not negate the matrix's broader Multipath status. Windows App versions and macOS Beta support remain platform-specific. Check the actual cloud/client/transport combination, permitted endpoints and negotiated connection before relying on a standby path. Multiple paths do not promise summed bandwidth or survival when every path fails. TURN remains a relay.
proposed_changes.reason: Replace stale phased Government TCP wording while preserving raw tab-scoped Shortpath qualification; no full-gate blocker implied.
proposed_changes.apply_note: Coordinator may already have integrated overlapping technical replacement; reconcile rather than duplicate.

The AZ-204 exam used to earn the latter retired July 31, 2026, so a new candidate should verify the currently accepted path before scheduling; AZ-104 remains an active route as of this review.
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown: **Credential prerequisite — checked October 28, 2026:** The [DevOps Engineer Expert profile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/devops-engineer/) still accepts Azure Administrator Associate or Azure Developer Associate. [Azure Developer Associate and its renewal assessment are retired](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/azure-developer/), with July 31, 2026 recorded in the [retirement list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/credential-retirement). New candidates can use the currently offered Azure Administrator Associate route; holders of an earlier Developer credential should verify its accepted status with Microsoft. Do not infer that an AI/cloud developer replacement is automatically an accepted prerequisite or that this retires AZ-400.

Catalog approval and template versioning determine what self-service can create. Start with the [cloud concepts outline](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/microsoft-azure-fundamentals-describe-cloud-concepts/), then read [Cost optimization options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/describe-cost-management-azure/7a-describe-cost-optimization-options) (published **4 minutes**) within the [management and governance path](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/describe-azure-management-governance/). Compare a stable server, a steady but changing compute mix and a restartable batch job. For each, record responsibility boundaries, utilization assumptions, interruption tolerance, a candidate pricing model and a measurement you need before committing spend. **About 45–75 minutes**, estimated for selected reading and this original three-workload worksheet; the four-minute unit time is reading only. **VERIFY CURRENT:** eligibility, term and actual prices in the service's current documentation/calculator. No subscription, commitment purchase or Azure deployment is required for the paper exercise; none was performed in this review.
practical_learning_routes.time_basis: Published unit/lab duration where stated; explicitly editorial estimate for original worksheet/review, excluding account setup and execution unless stated.
